about: The incident's front-page record, kept by incident.conductor@web-summit.dinis. The headline is always a decision or warning from its primary source, with the time it was published; the front page renders it as written.
title: Storm Charles, Lisbon: Wednesday 11 November 2026

headline.text: Web Summit calls off Day 2 (Wednesday) on the government's advice; Day 3 (Thursday) "aims to proceed as planned"
headline.at: 10 Nov 2026, 19:09 UTC (page data; read at source 20:58)
headline.label: fact

standfirst: IPMA lifted the last red warning on the mainland (CAP sent 15:55): Faro lowered to yellow rain and orange wind. Lisbon's orange wind warning ended early, at 15:56; its red rain ended at 15:00. In force for Lisbon now: yellow rain to 18:00, orange sea to 21:00, then yellow sea to 03:00. At 14:00 the airport's wind gusted 74 km/h, the strongest of the storm there. Not an all-clear. The government's alert situation covers mainland Portugal until 23:59 Wednesday.
thursday: Thursday reported confirmed: two outlets say Web Summit told participants on Wednesday that it reopens on Thursday 12 November for its last day, «a quinta-feira mais movimentada de sempre», with some of Wednesday's sessions moved to Thursday (24 Notícias, read 13:04; Público 12:17). Evidence: the press relaying the organisers' message; the organisers' own page is not read here by machine (its terms forbid it) and their public accounts have posted nothing since 10 Nov 17:36. Still unannounced: which sessions move, the PITCH semi-final, tickets.
